a1_subject: Life cycle for objects (timing and algorithm for taking part in continued execution)
a1_text: Life cycle for objects (timing and algorithm for taking part in continued execution). This item is required. This item need not be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (9.3.14.3, Life cycle for instance objects)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 113) 'Life cycle for objects (timing and algorithm for taking part in continued execution). This item is required. This item need not be documented in the implementor's user documentation.' -> §9.3.14.3 'An instance object is destroyed either when it is determined that the object cannot take part in the continued execution of the run unit, or when the run unit terminates, whichever occurs first. The timing and algorithm for the mechanism that determines whether or not an instance object can take part in the continued execution of the run unit is implementor-defined.' Documentation not required (audit register documented=False), so the absent §7 row is correct. Behaviour: a COBOL object is a managed .NET instance deriving CobolObject; reachability is decided by the .NET tracing garbage collector (the NOTE's 'garbage collection'), timing nondeterministic as the rule permits; the only object-owned resource with observable destruction (a per-object instance file, §9.1.4) is closed by a re-armed finalizer on collection, with CobolFile.CloseAll() at run-unit termination as the 'whichever occurs first' backstop. Probe at pin: conformance golden 2002/oo_object_file_two_instances re-run, output identical. Empty test-ref: no spec-derived test pins collection timing (it is implementor-defined and nondeterministic, so no test can). No owning note. cite.py --check 9.3.14.3 'The timing and algorithm for the mechanism that determines whether or not an instance object can take part in the continued execution of the run unit is implementor-defined' -> OK §9.3.14.3. || REFUTER OVERTURN (CONFORMS -> PARTIAL): Doc: A.1 item 113 need not be documented (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:34452). cite.py: 'OK §9.3.14.3 (Life cycle for instance objects) The timing and algorithm ... is implementor-defined.'; 'OK §9.1.4 (Open mode) — For file connectors in an object when the object is deleted.' The adjudicator's mechanism ('per-object instance files are closed by a re-armed finalizer') is DEAD CODE. ~CobolObject (src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/CobolObject.cs) calls CobolFile.EnqueueInstanceClose → `_reg => RunUnit.Current.Files` (CobolFile.cs:17), and RunUnit.Current is `_current.Value ??= new RunUnit()` over an AsyncLocal (RunUnit.cs). The GC finalizer thread does not carry the mutator's ExecutionContext, so it MINTS AN ORPHAN RunUnit and enqueues there; FileRegistry.DrainPendingObjectCloses on the real run unit never sees the key. Proof harness /tmp/adj/refute/h/P.cs (references the built Cobol.Net.Runtime.dll; subclass calls __TrackInstanceFile, GC.Collect+WaitForPendingFinalizers): output 'finalizer-thread ambient: a DIFFERENT (orphan) RunUnit; orphan pending=1' / 'main-run-unit pending closes after GC = 0'. COBOL-observable: /tmp/adj/refute/gc2.cob (--std 2002): loop {NEW WCLS; method W does OPEN OUTPUT of its instance file gc.dat + WRITE (no CLOSE); SET A TO NULL; 1,500,000 throwaway NEW JCLS} → 'K=00000002 OPEN-OUTPUT=61' — the second object's OPEN is refused as a sharing conflict by the first, unreachable object's connector, and stays refused forever. /tmp/adj/refute/gc1.cob: after dropping the writer and ~4M allocations, main OPEN INPUT of gc.dat → READ=10 (the record 'AAA' never flushed; the connector was never closed). So an object the runtime HAS determined cannot take part (its finalizer ran) is never destroyed as COBOL observes destruction (§9.1.4's implicit CLOSE 'when the object is deleted') until run-unit end, and FileRegistry keeps every minted per-object connector (and its OS handle) alive for the life of the run unit — unbounded growth for programs creating file-owning objects. §9.3.14.3 sentence 1 requires destruction 'when it is determined'; the §9.1.4 NOTE licenses GC delay, not a close that can never happen. Run-unit-end CloseAll still closes them (the 'whichever occurs first' backstop holds), and file-less objects are reclaimed correctly by the GC — hence PARTIAL, not DIVERGES. Tests: test-ref empty; golden 2002/oo_object_file_two_instances only covers explicitly CLOSEd/live objects and cannot see this. No kb/Work note found for the orphan-RunUnit finalizer (grep 'AsyncLocal|orphan|finalizer' over kb/Work) — needs a new defect note (areas runtime/oo + runtime/io; sibling sweep: any other finalizer/threadpool callback reaching RunUnit.Current). Static registries otherwise checked: CobolSort.Files, PointerImage.s_nameBases, collation caches hold no object references; PointerImage.s_areaBases is a ConditionalWeakTable. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1532, PB1535. || code-location commentary (registrar-normalized, kb/Work PB1522): src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/CobolObject.cs#CobolObject (GC.SuppressFinalize / __TrackInstanceFile / finalizer) | .NET garbage collector | src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/RunUnit.cs#Current (AsyncLocal)

a1_text: Listings (whether and when produced by the compiler, effect of logical conversion). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (6.5, Logical conversion; Clause 7, Compiler directing facility; 7.3.18, LISTING directive, General rule 1)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 117 'Listings (whether and when produced by the compiler, effect of logical conversion). This item is required. This item shall be documented... (6.5, Logical conversion; Clause 7...; 7.3.18, LISTING directive, General rule 1)' (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 117)). §7.3.18.3 GR1 'Whether the compiler produces a source listing is implementor-defined. If the compiler does not produce a source listing, the LISTING directive shall be ignored.' (cite.py --check 7.3.18.3 -> OK §7.3.18.3 1); NB the Annex's '7.3.18 ... General rule 1' lives in subclause .3). §6.5 'The implementor shall define the effect on the source listing, if any, of logical conversion.' (cite.py --check 6.5 -> OK §6.5 9)). Code: COBOL.NET produces NO source listing - the CLI (cobol --help) has no listing option and no listing writer exists in src; >>LISTING is recognized and held as NONE HELD in DirectiveStateRegistry citing §7.3.18.3 GR1; probe lst.cob (>>LISTING OFF / >>PAGE / >>LISTING ON, --std 2023) compiles clean and prints HI. So 'whether' = never, 'when' = never, and the logical-conversion effect is vacuous - a coherent determination. a1_subject: Locale specification (how user and system defaults defined; at least one user and one system default)
a1_text: Locale specification (how user and system defaults defined; at least one user and one system default). This item is required. This item need not be documented in the implementor's user documentation. The implementor may specify that the user locale and the system locale are the same locale. (8.2, Locales)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 118 'Locale specification (how user and system defaults defined; at least one user and one system default). This item is required. This item need not be documented in the implementor's user documentation. The implementor may specify that the user locale and the system locale are the same locale. (8.2, Locales)' (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 118)). §8.2.1: 'The implementor shall specify the manner in which the user default locale is defined and shall provide at least one user default locale for use in computing environments that do not provide a user default locale' and the SYSTEM twin (both cite.py --check 8.2.1 -> OK §8.2.1). No documentation obligation, so part (a) is waived (there is no '| DOC-A.1-118 |' row; the manner IS nevertheless written voluntarily: CONFORMANCE.md §4 A.4.9 locale paragraph 'the user default from COBOL_USER_LOCALE (else the process culture, else the root)', RuntimeConfig.All's COBOL_USER_LOCALE / COBOL_SYSTEM_LOCALE entries, DESIGN-locale-facility §4.3 table, DETERMINATION L2 = owner decision Q2). Part (b), the behaviour: LocaleState() sets UserDefault = Determine(COBOL_USER_LOCALE, CultureInfo.CurrentCulture) and SystemDefault = Determine(COBOL_SYSTEM_LOCALE, CultureInfo.InstalledUICulture); Determine returns the env value, else the culture name, else '' (the root) when the host has no culture data - so at least one user and one system default ALWAYS exist, including environments that supply none. SystemDefault has no setter (§8.2.1 'The capability of setting the system default locale from COBOL is not provided'). Probe loc.cob (--std 2023; SET LOCALE LC_ALL TO SYSTEM-DEFAULT / USER-DEFAULT then FUNCTION LOCALE-DATE): env COBOL_USER_LOCALE=de-DE COBOL_SYSTEM_LOCALE=fr-FR -> SYS 24/09/2026, USR 24.09.2026 (two distinct defaults, each honoured); env unset + DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_INVARIANT=1 -> both 09/24/2026, no exception, rc 0 (the root fallback). Tests: the unit test SetFromSystemDefault asserts CurrentLocale == SystemDefault; pb64t1_set_locale_categories runs SYSDEF/USERDEF arms under the harness's pinned INVARIANT defaults. Caveat for the refuter: no test pins the unset-env culture fallback arm (it is host-dependent by design); verified by probe only. Editions: the locale facility (A.4.9) is 2002+. Owning note: none (grep item 118: none); design owner kb/Work PB64 (landed T1). || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1535.

a1_subject: Locale specification (manner of implementation)
a1_text: Locale specification (manner of implementation). This item is required because at least one default locale is required. This item does not have to be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.2, Locales)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 119 'Locale specification (manner of implementation). This item is required because at least one default locale is required. This item does not have to be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.2, Locales)' (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 119)). §8.2.1: 'The format and implementation of locales may differ from those specifications provided that logically-equivalent functionality is supported.' and 'If the operating environment does not supply a default locale, it is implementor-defined.' (both cite.py --check 8.2.1 -> OK §8.2.1). No documentation obligation, so part (a) is waived (no '| DOC-A.1-119 |' row; the manner is nevertheless described voluntarily in CONFORMANCE.md §4's A.4.9 locale paragraph and docs/rearchitecture/DESIGN-locale-facility.md). Part (b): a locale IS implemented and a default always exists - locales are identified by BCP 47/CLDR tags normalized by LocaleIdentification (availability = CollationEngine.IsKnownLocale), with per-category state in LocaleState (LC_COLLATE, LC_CTYPE, LC_MESSAGES, LC_MONETARY, LC_NUMERIC, LC_TIME), collation from COBOL.NET's own derived CLDR 48 / UCA 17 tables and the LC_MONETARY/LC_NUMERIC/LC_TIME facts read once per locale by LocaleFacts from the nearest predefined .NET culture; the root locale ('') is the implementor-supplied default when the environment supplies none (LocaleState.Determine). A.4.9 is CLAIMED WHOLE in CONFORMANCE.md §4. Probe loc.cob: SET LOCALE to SYSTEM-DEFAULT / USER-DEFAULT + LOCALE-DATE works with env-named defaults (fr-FR / de-DE formats differ) and with invariant globalization and no env (root, rc 0). Editions: 2002+ (the locale facility). Owning note: none (grep item 119: none); design owner kb/Work PB64. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1535.

a1_subject: Locale switch (whether a switch by a non-COBOL runtime module is recognized by COBOL)
a1_text: Locale switch (whether a switch by a non-COBOL runtime module is recognized by COBOL). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for activation of non-COBOL runtime modules. This item, if provided, shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.2, Locales)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 120 'Locale switch (whether a switch by a non-COBOL runtime module is recognized by COBOL). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for activation of non-COBOL runtime modules. This item, if provided, shall be documented... (8.2, Locales)' (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 120)). §8.2.1: 'It is implementor-defined whether, and for which locale categories, a switch of current locale by a non-COBOL runtime module is utilized by COBOL.' (cite.py --check 8.2.1 -> OK §8.2.1). CONDITION: COBOL.NET cannot CALL a non-COBOL program (DOC-A.1-19 / §3), but CONFORMANCE.md §3 declares a .NET host activating a generated program a supported non-COBOL activator (kb/Work PB408), and that host is a non-COBOL runtime module in the run unit that can switch Thread.CurrentCulture - so the question arises and the item is taken as incurred (same reading wave 1 applied to DOC-A.1-65). Code fixes the answer: DETERMINATION L3 (docs/rearchitecture/DESIGN-locale-facility.md §4.3: 'COBOL.NET never observes a foreign switch - LocaleState is authoritative and is read from CultureInfo once, at run-unit activation'); LocaleState() reads CurrentCulture/InstalledUICulture once and nothing in src/Cobol.Net.Runtime re-reads CurrentCulture during a run unit (grep: only LocaleState's ctor and LocaleConfig.DefaultLocale, the latter used by CollationRuntime only when RunUnit.TryCurrent is null, i.e. outside any run unit). So the answer is 'no category is utilized'. CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-120 |' row, and the §4 A.4.9 locale paragraph says the defaults are read at activation but never states the foreign-switch rule; the only statement is in the design doc, which is not the user documentation -> DIVERGES (harm silent). Not probed with a host that switches culture mid-run-unit (requires building a separate .NET host; the brief forbids builds on this VM) - verified by reading. Editions: 2002+ (locales). Owning note: none item-specific (grep 'item 120' / 'DOC-A.1-120': none); umbrella kb/Work A11 / PB160; design owner PB64. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1534, PB1535.

a1_text: National literals (number of hexadecimal digits that map to a national character). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.3.3.5, National literals, Syntax rule 5)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 122 'National literals (number of hexadecimal digits that map to a national character). This item is required. This item shall be documented... (8.3.3.5, National literals, Syntax rule 5)' (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 122)). §8.3.3.5.3 SR5: 'Each hex-character-sequence-1 shall consist of the number of hexadecimal digits that the implementor has specified as the number of hexadecimal digits that map to a national character.' (cite.py --check 8.3.3.5.3 -> OK §8.3.3.5.3 5); the Annex's '8.3.3.5' is the parent). Code fixes the number at FOUR (one UTF-16 code unit, determination D-N1): CobolLiteral.HexGroupViolation reports COBOLNET1635 for a digit count that is not a multiple of 4, and the decoder maps each 4-digit group to one national character. a1_subject: Native arithmetic (when an operand or arithmetic expression is an integer)
a1_text: Native arithmetic (when an operand or arithmetic expression is an integer). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (5.5, Integer operands)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 124 'Native arithmetic (when an operand or arithmetic expression is an integer). This item is required. This item shall be documented... (5.5, Integer operands)' (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 124)). §5.5 3) a): 'If native arithmetic is in effect, the implementor shall define when the operand represents an integer.' (cite.py --check 5.5 -> OK §5.5 3) a)). Native arithmetic is COBOL.NET's default mode. Code fixes a determination at every runtime integer test: the operand is an integer iff its exact value has no nonzero fractional digit - CobolNum.HasFraction(unscaled, scale) on the scaled-Int128 native intermediate (DOC-A.1-123), used by the subscript test (CobolTable.OccScaled -> EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT 'is not an integer (ISO 8.4.2.3.4 GR1b)'), reference modification (CobolString), SET index/amount (CobolIndex: 'A NaN or an infinity is not an integer'), and a floating-point operand of integral value counts as an integer. Probes int1.cob / int2.cob (--std 2023): E(I / 2) and S(I / 2:1) with I=4 -> 'W B'; COMP-2 F = 2.0 as subscript / refmod -> 'W B' (integral float accepted); I=5 with >>TURN EC-BOUND CHECKING ON -> 'EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT (fatal): subscript value 2.500000000 is not an integer'; with checking off the 2.5 subscript silently selects element 2 (no EXCEPTION-STATUS) - an undocumented consequence of the same determination. At compile time the §5.5 2) static screen is separate (COBOLNET1627 refuses FACTORIAL(I / 2) and FACTORIAL(COMP-2) outright). CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-124 |' row; DOC-A.1-123 (the native intermediate) states the representation but never says when a value represents an integer -> DIVERGES (harm silent). Owning note: none (grep 'item 124' / 'DOC-A.1-124' / '§5.5 3': none); umbrella kb/Work A11 / PB160. Editions: native arithmetic and runtime integer operands exist in every edition. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1534, PB1535.

a1_text: NULL (value of NULL). This item is required. This item need not be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.4.3.7, NULL object reference, General rule 1; 8.4.3.10, NULL address pointer and message tag content, General rules 1, 2, and 3)

Documentation NOT required, so (a) is vacuous; CONFORMANCE.md has no row and needs none. Behaviour: object ref NULL = CLR null (never references an object); data-pointer/program-pointer/function-pointer NULL = each readonly struct's default, distinct from any real address. Probe: DP initial = NULL, SET DP TO ADDRESS OF X -> NOT = NULL, SET DP TO NULL -> = NULL, NULL=NULL, PP initial NULL. pb557 golden asserts P NOT = NULL after ADDRESS OF (the 'guaranteed not to represent the address of any data item' half). GR4 message-tag NULL: USAGE MESSAGE-TAG is the declined MCS facility (CONFORMANCE §4 item 1, COBOLNET1943) - outside the claim. cite: OK §8.4.3.7.4 1) '...a unique value defined by the implementor such that it is guaranteed to never reference an object'; OK §8.4.3.10.4 1) 'The null data address is an implementor-defined value that is guaranteed not to represent the address of any data item'; OK §A.1 125).
